newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares surge nearly six pct.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares surge nearly six pct.

text.p: Istanbul shares surged an average 5.93 percent on Wednesday in a very strong reaction to Tuesday's 3.98 percent dive, amid heavy selective buys led by shares of largely state-owned firms, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 closed 4,733.73 points higher at 84,595.12. Trade volume was little changed at 28.11 trillion lira ($283 million) after Tuesday's 28.21 trillion ($284 million).

Brokers said renewed privatisation hopes caused players to focus on state shares which are on the government's 1997 selloff programme and can move the market index sharply due to their high market capitalisations.

"I do not approve yesterday's and today's sharp movements. The possibility of a downtrend still exists because the market has not yet digested the recent rally," said Kursat Oral from Meksa securities.

The index surged 29.3 percent from September 13 to October 23 in a strong uptrend, but has since drifted mostly between 81,000 and 84,000 as it failed in three attempts to pierce the critical 85,000 barrier.
It hit an all-time high close of 84,692.20 on November 11 and sank to 79,861.38 on Tuesday.
